column3: A Russian Orthodox church with a big green onion dome and red brick walls, built in the early 20th century. It is the symbol of Harbin and sits in a lively square.
A cobbled pedestrian street lined with European-style buildings from the early 1900s, full of cafés, shops and street performers.
Every winter, workers build a huge park of glowing towers, castles and slides out of blocks of ice cut from the Songhua River. It lights up in rainbow colors at night.
A leafy island park in the Songhua River, with lawns, lakes and villas. It is a summer escape and a winter snow sculpture show.
Harbin's river, wide and slow in summer and frozen thick enough in winter for skating, sledding and ice sculptures.
A park that breeds Siberian tigers, the largest big cats, which you can watch from a bus as they roam outside.
A museum on the site of a Japanese wartime biological weapons unit, and a solemn reminder of the war's suffering.
An aquarium and polar park, where you can see polar bears, penguins and beluga whales in the cold north.
Crispy slices of pork coated in a sweet and sour glaze, said to have been invented in Harbin for Russian guests. It is the signature dish of the northeast.
Harbin's smoked red sausage has a Russian-style recipe, with a garlicky, smoky flavor, and is sold in shops everywhere.
A creamy ice cream bar sold on Central Street from a hotel since the 1900s, eaten even in winter in freezing weather.
A big, round, dense loaf of bread in the Russian style, with a crisp crust, which is often sold at old bakeries in Harbin.
One of the oldest beer brands in China, first brewed in Harbin in 1900 by a Czech-Polish entrepreneur.
Pears frozen outside in winter until they turn black, then thawed in cold water, soft, icy and sweet.
A hearty winter feast of pork, blood sausage, pickled cabbage and potatoes cooked together, traditionally eaten after a pig is slaughtered.
Harbin's annual winter festival, with ice sculptures, snow carving contests and winter swimming in the Songhua River.
Many of the city's buildings, foods and customs recall the Russians who came to build the railway and to settle here.
Lanterns carved from ice, with a candle or LED inside, were a folk tradition among the people of the northeast long before the festival.
A vast wetland and nature reserve where red-crowned cranes nest every year, one of the best places to see them.
Meat grilled at the table over charcoal, with its own style of dipping sauce, a lively local meal.
The red-crowned crane is a symbol of long life in China, and Qiqihar is proud to be its home.
A long mountain lake formed by volcanic lava that blocked a river, with a green bank and a waterfall at the north end.
A wide waterfall at the outflow of Jingpo Lake, which pours over a lava rim into a deep pool.
A mountain village famous for its heavy snowfall, with thick, soft caps of snow on the roofs of its wooden houses.
A hamlet in the mountains where snow piles up on the roofs and visitors come in winter to see it by lantern light.
Chewy cold noodles in a tangy, sweet and sour broth with beef and pickled vegetables. They are part of the Korean heritage of the area.
A prized rice grown near Wuchang in rich black soil, known for its fragrance and sticky texture.
Ethnic Koreans have lived here for generations, and their food, dance, clothing and festivals are part of local life.
The Hezhe people of the Amur region traditionally made clothes and crafts from fish skin, a rare skill.
Salmon swim up the Amur and Ussuri rivers each autumn. Fuyuan is known for its fresh salmon and red roe.
Fish grilled and then simmered in a spicy sauce with vegetables, a popular dish for sharing.
Lamb raised on Dumo's grasslands is tender, with little gamey taste, and is cooked in stews and barbecue.
A bridge across the Amur River, which marks the border between China and Russia, and connects the cities of Heihe and Blagoveshchensk.
A park of dormant volcanoes, black lava fields, and five linked lakes. It is a UNESCO Global Geopark.
Mineral water from the volcanic springs is slightly fizzy with a distinctive taste, sold across China.
The northernmost village in China, in Mohe, where summer nights are very short, and in winter it is bitterly cold.
On rare clear nights in summer, green lights can dance in the sky above Mohe, the best place in China to see the aurora.
Wild blueberries grow in the northern forests and are picked in summer, often used for jam and wine.
The Ewenki people raise reindeer in the Greater Khingan forests, and the animals are central to their culture.
A small people of the northeast forests who traditionally lived by hunting and wore clothes of skins.
A forest of tall Korean pines in Yichun, which provide wood and big pine nuts and are the symbol of the Lesser Khingan range.
Pine nuts from Korean pines are large and rich, and are a snack and an ingredient across the northeast.
A sweet, deep purple wine made from wild blueberries of the northern forests.
A river that forms part of the border with Russia and is known for its salmon and for a famous folk song.
Rice grown on the black soil of the Sanjiang Plain, with a sweet and soft grain.
A huge forested range in the far north of China, with larch trees, rivers and wildlife, and cold winters.
